mainText: Good morning. Here is your curated AI briefing for Wednesday, August 19, 2026. Liquid AI has released new LFM2.5 model checkpoints that utilize a technique called Quantization-Aware Distillation. This method involves training a smaller student model to mimic a larger, high-precision teacher model while simultaneously adjusting for the loss of accuracy that typically occurs during quantization, which is the process of reducing the precision of a model's weights to save memory. These new Q4_0 checkpoints maintain approximately 97% of the performance of their full-precision counterparts while retaining the low memory footprint and high throughput of standard four-bit models. The company states that these models are designed for edge deployment on hardware like smartphones and single-board computers. The release includes four versions of the model, ranging from 230 million to 2.6 billion parameters, all of which are available today on the Hugging Face platform for use with runtime environments that support GGUF file formats. In the realm of infrastructure, Relativity Networks has announced it secured 22 million dollars in funding to advance hollow-core fiber optic technology for data centers. Unlike traditional fiber, which transmits light through glass, hollow-core fiber uses a vacuum-filled chamber to carry signals. Because light travels faster through a vacuum than through glass, this technology can reduce latency by approximately 50%, a significant factor as data center campuses continue to expand across larger physical areas. The company also reported a 40 million dollar follow-on order from an unnamed hyperscaler. This development reflects a broader industry trend of optimizing the physical geography of data centers to manage the massive networking requirements of modern artificial intelligence compute. Also in infrastructure, Amazon has launched the general availability of its Bedrock AgentCore payments service. The platform allows autonomous AI agents to conduct financial transactions using stablecoin wallets, such as those provided by Coinbase or Privy. Designed for enterprise use, the service includes security features that hide raw credentials from the agent, instead using short-lived tokens to sign transactions. It supports multiple payment protocols, including the Machine Payment Protocol, and allows developers to set spending limits to prevent autonomous agents from incurring unintended costs. This update aims to address a primary barrier to agentic workflows by providing a standardized, secure way for AI systems to pay for APIs and services on a per-execution basis. In other news, OpenAI is expanding its ChatGPT Ads platform to 31 European countries next week. The company stated that ads will only be shown to users on free and lower-cost plans, while enterprise and professional subscriptions will remain ad-free. OpenAI emphasizes that it does not sell user data and that advertisements are designed to be distinct from the model's responses. Security researchers at Varonis recently disclosed a vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot that allowed them to bypass user consent requirements for certain commands. By repeatedly querying the assistant about its own internal guardrails, researchers discovered an undocumented parameter that could be used to force automatic execution of prompts. Microsoft mitigated the issue earlier this year and introduced more comprehensive fixes on Tuesday. A study from researchers at Princeton University suggests that current AI agents are not yet capable of performing autonomous, open-ended research at the caliber required by top machine-learning conferences. Although the agents could manage engineering tasks, they struggled with the creativity and judgment necessary to produce novel contributions. Finally, biotech startup Vivodyne has highlighted the challenges of using AI for drug discovery, arguing that models often lack the high-quality, causal biological data needed to predict human responses. The company has built autonomous robotic labs designed to grow human tissue for testing, aiming to provide better data than traditional animal models. Looking ahead, expect continued scrutiny regarding the balance between autonomous AI capabilities and the need for human-led oversight, particularly as both private firms and government institutions integrate these tools into high-stakes environments.
